privacy.title: Privacy Policy
summary: No accounts, no cookies, no analytics, no tracking.
We don't collect personal data. Your browser does contact the hosting and content services listed below.
The only thing stored on your device is your light/dark theme choice.

p: CommonGlot is an open project that publishes language technology resources and a directory of languages and scripts at commonglot.github.io. The site is static: it has no server of its own, no user accounts and no forms.

Nothing. We do not run analytics, advertising or tracking scripts, and we do not set cookies. Search terms and filters you use in the directories are processed entirely in your browser; they appear in the page address so you can share a view, but they are not sent to us.

The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. When you visit, GitHub receives standard request information such as your IP address, browser type and the page requested, and may keep it in server logs for security and operations. We cannot access these logs.

To display pages, your browser loads some files directly from these providers. Each receives your IP address and browser details, and handles them under its own privacy policy. Our pages only send the site's origin (not the full page address) as the referrer.

list.label: Google Fonts
list.text: Typefaces for the site and, on script pages, fonts for rare writing systems.

list.label: cdnjs (Cloudflare)
list.text: The Leaflet map library, on pages with maps.

list.label: OpenStreetMap
list.text: Fallback map tiles if CARTO tiles are unavailable.

p: If you switch between light and dark mode, the choice is saved in your browser's local storage under the key “cg-theme”. It never leaves your device. You can remove it by clearing site data in your browser.
Pages link to external sites such as GitHub, Hugging Face, Glottolog and Ethnologue. Their privacy practices are their own; please read their policies when you visit them.
The site is suitable for all ages and collects no personal data from anyone, including children.

Because we hold no personal data about you, there is nothing for us to access, correct or delete. For data processed by GitHub or the providers above, please contact them directly. Questions about this policy are welcome through GitHub issues.
If we change how the site handles data, we will update this page and its date. The full history of this page is public in the site's GitHub repository.

p: By using commonglot.github.io you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.

CommonGlot presents information about the GlotSuite research projects and a directory of languages and writing systems, including what language technology supports each one. It is an informational resource maintained by an open project.

The language and script directory is compiled from the sources below. Each source keeps its own licence, and some (such as Glottolog's CC BY 4.0) require attribution. If you reuse the data, please credit the original sources as well as CommonGlot.

Models, datasets and tools linked from project pages are released by their authors under their own licences, stated in each project's repository or dataset card. Datasets built from web text may contain material owned by third parties; check each dataset's terms before use.

Directory information is generated automatically from public sources and may be incomplete, out of date or wrong. Language names, classifications and endangerment statuses reflect those sources, not an official position of CommonGlot. Do not rely on the site for decisions where errors could cause harm. Corrections are welcome.
Please do not attempt to disrupt the site or the services it relies on. Automated access is fine, but for bulk use download the JSON files or clone the repository instead of crawling every page.

Maps, fonts and libraries are provided by third parties (see the Privacy Policy), and links lead to external sites. Their use is subject to their own terms; we are not responsible for their content or availability.
The CommonGlot logo and the names and logos of GlotSuite projects identify those projects. You may use them to refer to the projects, but not in a way that suggests endorsement without permission.
